en: PAGASA Wind Signal No. 1 means winds up to 61 kilometers per hour are expected, so you must secure loose roof materials.
A heat index above 42 degrees Celsius causes severe heat stroke, so you must drink water and stay indoors.
Rubber-soled shoes do not protect you from lightning strikes, so seek shelter inside a fully enclosed building or metal-topped vehicle.
Washing hands after playing in soil prevents infection by hookworm larvae that can penetrate bare skin and cause illness.
Pumice is a lightweight volcanic rock often used as a natural exfoliant to safely remove dead skin from your feet.
Collecting rainwater in clean containers provides a good water source, but it must be boiled to kill bacteria before drinking.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses can cause permanent eye damage called solar retinopathy.
During a spring tide, higher high tides occur, so beachgoers must stay away from the water to avoid being swept away.
The North Star, also known as Polaris, always points north, helping lost hikers navigate safely at night.
Ultraviolet rays from the sun are strongest between 10 AM and 4 PM, requiring sunscreen to prevent skin damage.
During an earthquake, dropping to the ground and covering your head under a sturdy table prevents injuries from falling debris.
Wearing a mask when sweeping dry volcanic ash prevents inhaling fine particles that can severely irritate your lungs.
